briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-012
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- office roof: (-11, -57), roof
- electrical room: (-44, 94), indoor
- workcell West: (6, 35), indoor
- east fence: (-130, -126), outdoor
- water tank: (-84, -125), outdoor

Robots:
- A1 (fixed_arm): installed at workcell West and cannot move; it can only work on tasks located at workcell West. Equipment: robotic arm. Mains-powered (no endurance limit).
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg), thermal camera. Endurance: 1140 s, including the return to its start.
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 7 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3060 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Run a thermal scan of office roof. Location: office roof. Duration: 150 s. Needs: thermal camera.
- T2: Deliver the replacement filter (7 kg) to electrical room. Location: electrical room. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 7 kg).
- T3: Deliver the pressure gauge (7 kg) to east fence. Location: east fence. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 7 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 660 s.
- T4: Deliver the first-aid kit (2 kg) to electrical room. Location: electrical room. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 2 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.
- T5: Run a thermal scan of office roof. Location: office roof. Duration: 210 s. Needs: thermal camera. Deadline: finished by t = 360 s.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 900 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Here's what we need from the robots today.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: office roof (-11, -57, a rooftop); electrical room (-44, 94, indoors); workcell West (6, 35, indoors); east fence (-130, -126, outside); water tank (-84, -125, outside).

The fleet: A1 is a robot arm bolted down in workcell West; it can't move but can work on jobs inside workcell West, and it runs on mains power. D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera and a thermal camera; it flies at 8.5 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 19 minutes including the flight home. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 7 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 51 minutes including getting back.

Jobs:
(T1) Check office roof for hot spots - that takes 2.5 minutes on site.
(T2) Get the replacement filter (7 kg) over to electrical room - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T3) Get the pressure gauge (7 kg) over to east fence - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 11 minutes.
(T4) Drop the first-aid kit off at electrical room; it weighs 2 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.
(T5) Check office roof for hot spots - that takes 3.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 6 minutes.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 15 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
